segments.he: מהרי"צ ר' לייב מסטרעסטיניץ ששאל אותו הרה"צ ר' נחום מטשערנאביל זצ"ל מדוע אין לו לאכטער וענה לו הר' לייב הנ"ל אצלי הלאכטער הם נע נד ואני יושב במקומי ואצליכם הוא להיפך שאתם נע ונד והלאכטער הם במקומם. "בייא אייך זענין דיא לה?? אין איהה זאט נע ונד (כדי שיהי' לו פרנסה ולאכטער וכו') אין בא מיר בין איך אוף דעם ?? אין ד?? ??. זענין נע ונד (היינו שחשוב אצלו איפה שהם כאלו הם אצלו ואינו כדאי לו שיהא נע ונד בשביל זה:
segments.en:
A certain woman — a truly righteous woman — told me that she was the eldest granddaughter of Reb Shmuel the Alef. Once she did him a great favor: his grandson, her uncle named Reb Avner, had Reb Shmuel prophesy over him even when he saw his daughter pregnant with him — he said to her: "You have conceived from a great soul — the soul of Avner son of Ner." And he was very precious in Reb Shmuel's eyes. Once when the boy was small he became upset and nothing could appease him — and this caused Reb Shmuel distress. She went and appeased him until he was calmed. When Reb Shmuel saw this he said to her: "For the good you have done me in this — I bless you that you will never suffer from stomach ailments, and whatever foods you eat will not harm you." And so it has been to this day — no food harms her and she has never suffered from stomach ailments.

Reb Avner told: when he was in Glupin, he made a siyum on the entire Talmud and made a feast with musical instruments. And he told his father that Reb Shmuel lived in the lower room and his son Reb Avraham — who was a great and wondrous person — lived in the upper room, closed and sealed there in the service of Hashem. And it was written in a handwritten manuscript of the Alshich that whoever studied the entire Alshich such and such times, the Alshich would come and study with him. Reb Avraham fulfilled this — studying the Alshich many times — and when he finished in the upper room he said: "Let our master fulfill what he promised." Suddenly the Alshich stood before him in a bright and beautiful form, radiant as the sun — beyond what he could endure — and Reb Avraham's face changed color and he could not speak. He immediately descended to his father Reb Shmuel and fell faint. They revived him and he told Reb Shmuel what had happened. Reb Shmuel said to him: "What is the novelty in this for you, and why were you so frightened?" [For Reb Shmuel was accustomed to such things.] Reb Shmuel was blind — and would play the violin and would not sleep sixty breaths [a very short sleep] at any one time. And they told me: I was a small child in his time and I would smell a fragrance literally like perfume from him [because my mother used to eat esrogim when she was pregnant with me]. And they would bring me to him in his lap and he would hold me in his lap and smell from me — and this gave him great pleasure. And every day they were required to bring me to him so he could smell from me.

My father told me that my grandfather Reb Yitzchak — my mother's father — son-in-law of Reb Shmuel, was a very sharp and great Gaon, well-versed in the entire Rambam with great sharpness and erudition. Before his passing, my father sat by his bedside — and suddenly he awakened and commanded that the Rambam be brought. He looked at it and said: "Good, good!" My father asked what this was. He answered: "Just now the Rambam came to me in a waking state and told me: because throughout all your days you studied greatly in my book Mishneh Torah — I have now come at the time of your passing to resolve for you all the difficulties you have in the Rambam." And he asked him what was difficult for him, and resolved it. Therefore he commanded that the Rambam be brought — to see if it was indeed resolved — and he saw that it was well resolved.
